key_insight: This paper shows that e-commerce search should not only find exact matches, but also surface related items that users are likely to want next. By generating intent-aware expansions, the system improves discoverability of substitutes, complements, and thematically similar products.
problem_solved: Traditional search engines over-optimize for precision and miss items that are useful but not textually identical to the query. This is especially harmful in grocery and marketplace settings where users benefit from related products, alternatives, and add-ons.
method: Use intent-conditioned recall expansion to generate related queries or item signals from the original search intent.
Augment the retrieval stage so the search system can surface substitute, complementary, and thematically related items beyond exact keyword matches.
Design the approach to be scalable for production e-commerce search environments.
impact: For ML practitioners, this highlights a practical way to move beyond exact-match retrieval and improve both user satisfaction and business outcomes. It is especially relevant for building discovery-oriented search systems in domains where intent is broader than the literal query.

paper_title: Improving Item Discoverability in e-Commerce Search via Related Intent Generation
paper_authors: Ji Xin, Xiao Xiao, Ishan Bhatt, Vinesh Gudla, Trace Levinson
